hook_text: Nguni herders have hundreds of names for cattle patterns. Every cow is one species — and none are the same.
clip_script: Look at a herd of Nguni cattle: white with black spots, red speckles, patterns named after birds and eggs. All one species, because they can breed and their calves can breed too. A horse and a donkey can make a mule, but mules cannot breed, so those are two species. Now look at your class. Line everyone up by height: it changes smoothly, no jumps. That is continuous variation, and its graph makes a hill. Ask blood groups: A, B, AB or O, nothing in between. Discontinuous variation, separate bars. Where do differences come from? Genes, half from each parent in a new mix every time. And life: food, sun, sport. A scar or gym muscles will never be passed on. And variation is a survival tool: when a new disease arrives, the different ones may make it.
visual_style: A whiteboard herd with every cow uniquely patterned; a class line-up morphing into a bell curve; four separate blood-group bars; a DNA mix-up animation.
pacing: Colourful opening, two quick graph reveals, a punchy survival message.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure the variation in your own class.
